name: Molniya + Tundra (HEO 63.4°)
description: High-eccentricity orbits at 63.4° critical inclination. Molniya (12-hour, 600 × 40,000 km) — Russian high-latitude comms + Oko/Meridian early warning since 1965. Tundra (24-hour, ~25,000 × ~47,000 km) — Sirius XM Satellite Radio + US SBIRS-HEO sensors.
scale_fact: The 63.4° inclination is no accident — it's the 'critical inclination' where Earth's J2 perturbation locks the apogee in place over the chosen hemisphere.
